Reconsideration of this Application and entry of this Amendment is respectfully requested. The present Amendment replies to a Non-Final Office Action of November 19, 2024. Claims 1-22 are pending in the present Application. Claim 22 was allowed, claims 10-11 and 18 were found allowable if rewritten in independent form. By this Amendment claims 1, 3, 7, 10, 14-17, and 20-21 are amended, and claim 18 is canceled. In the Office Action, the Examiner rejected the claims on various grounds. Applicant responds to the rejections as subsequently recited herein.
Drawings
The drawings stand objected to under 37 CFR 1.84. Corrected drawings in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d) are enclosed.
The objection to the drawings has been overcome. Acceptance of the drawings and withdrawal of the objection is respectfully requested.
Claim Objections
Claims 1, 3, and 16 are amended as suggested.
The objection to the claims has been overcome. Withdrawal of the objection is respectfully requested.
35 U.S.C. § 112 Rejections
Claims 7, 14, 17, 20 and 21 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. @ 112(b)

Claims 7, 14, 17, and 20-21 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b). Claims 7, 14, 17, and 20-21 are amended to overcome the rejection. Applicant respectfully submits that the Q112 rejection of claims 7, 14, 17, and 20-21 has been overcome.
35 U.S.C. § 102 Rejections

An anticipation rejection 35 U.S.C. §102 requires that a single prior art reference discloses each and every element of the claimed invention and as arranged as in the claim (See MPEP @ 2131. "A claim is anticipated only if each and every element as set forth in the claim is found, either expressly or inherently described, in a single prior art reference." (MPEP 9 2131 citing Verdegaal Bros. v. Union Oil Co. of California, 814 F.2d 628, 631, 2 USPQ2d 1051, 1053 (Fed. Cir. 1987). "The identical invention must be shown in as complete detail as is contained in the ... claim." (MPEP @ 2131 citing Richardson v. Suzuki Motor Co., 868 F.2d 1226, 1236, 9 USPQ2d 1913, 1920 (Fed. Cir. 1989).
Applicant respectfully submits that the cited reference does not disclose each and every element of the claims as arranged therein.
Claims 1-5 and 13-14 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. 9 102(a)(1)
Amendment and Response
Page -2
Claims 1-5 and 13-14 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as being

anticipated by U.S. Pre-grant Publication No. 2021/0301797 to Allen (hereinafter "Allen"). Applicant respectfully submits that Allen does not disclose each and every element of the claimed invention as arranged as in the claim, and thus the §102 rejection of claims 1-5 and 13-14 has been overcome.

More specifically, claim 1 is amended to recite the allowable feature of claim 10, i.e., the "electron-emitting electrode". The Office Action provides that Allen discloses the "cathodes are used to collect the electrons and thus would not emit the electrons" (Office Action, pg. 16 citing Allen, para [0032]). Applicant respectfully submits that as Allen does not disclose each and every element of the claimed invention as arranged in claim 1 as amended, the Q102 rejection of claim 1 has been overcome.
Claims 2-5 and 13-14 depend from amended claim 1 and include all the features thereof. Claims 2-5 and 13-14 are allowable for all the reasons set forth for claim 1 above.
In light of the foregoing, Applicant contends that the claims listed above are not anticipated by Allen and respectfully requests withdrawal of the §102 rejections.
35 U.S.C. §103 Rejections

Obviousness is a question of law, based on the factual inquiries of 1) determining the scope and content of the prior art; 2) ascertaining the differences between the claimed invention and the prior art; and 3) resolving the level of ordinary skill in the pertinent art. Graham v John Deere Co., 383 U.S. 1, 148 USPQ 459 (1966). To establish prima facie obviousness of a claimed invention, all the claim features must be taught or suggested by the prior art. In re Royka, 490 F.2d 981, 180 USPQ 580 (CCPA 1974). See MPEP a §2143.03.
Applicant respectfully asserts that the cited references fail to teach or suggest all the claim features.
Claims 6-9, 12, 15-17 and 19-21 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. @ 103
Claims 6-9, 12, 15-17, and 19-21 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Alen in view of U.S. Patent No. 11,510,307 to Perricone

(Hereinafter "Perricone") Applicant respectfully submits that Allen, alone or in combination with Perricone, does not teach or suggest all the claim features, and thus the §103 rejection of claims 6-9, 12, 15-17, and 19-21 has been overcome.
Claims 6-9 and 12 depend from claim 1. Claim 1 is amended to recite the

allowable feature of claim 10, i.e., the "electron-emitting electrode". The Office Action provides that Allen discloses "the cathodes are used to collect the electrons and thus would not emit the electrons" (Office Action, pg. 16 citing Allen, para [0032]). Perricone does not make up for this lack of teaching or suggestion by Allen. Applicant respectfully submits that as Allen, alone or in combination with Perricone, does not teach or suggest all of the claimed features of claim 1, claim 1 as amended is allowable. Claims 6-9 and 12 depend from claim 1 and include all the features thereof. Claims 6-9 and 12 are allowable for all the reasons set forth for claim 1 above.
16-17 and 19-21 depend from claim 15. Claim 15 is amended to recite the

allowable feature of claim 18, i.e., the "at least one exit ring electrode biased positive' along with the remaining limitations of Claim 18 are not taught for fairly suggested in the prior art of record" (Office Action, pg. 16). Applicant respectfully submits that as neither Allen nor Perricone does not teach or suggest all the claimed features of claim 15 as amended, the §103 rejection of claim 15 has been overcome.
Claims 16-17 and 19-21 depend from amended claim 15 and include all the
features thereof. Claims 16-17 and 19-21 are allowable for all the reasons of claim 15 above.
In light of the foregoing, Applicant requests withdrawal of the §103 rejections.
